question.problem: The equation ${x}^{2}+4x+8=0$ can be written in the form $(x+p)^{2}=q.$ Find $p+q,$ and solve the equation.
question.worked_solution:
We first move the constant to the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+4x+8 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+4x & =-8\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we complete the square on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+4x & =-8 \\ {x}^{2}+2\cdot 2x+{2}^{2}-{2}^{2} & =-8 \\ (x+2)^{2}-4 & =-8 \\ (x+2)^{2} & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $p=2,\,q=-4,$ and $p+q=-2.$

Finally, we solve the equation using the square root method:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+2)^{2} & =-4 \\ x+2 & =\pm \sqrt{-4} \\ x+2 & =\pm 2\,\text{i} \\ x & =-2\pm 2\,\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation has two solutions, $x=-2+2\,\text{i}$ and $x=-2-2\,\text{i}.$
